pairs.evidence: app/_lib/voice/openai.ts:15 The OpenAI voice adapter chooses the realtime model from an environment variable inside the provider, so every session changes with no call-site parameter, no consumer, and no expiry.

techniques.evidence: app/_lib/voice/minute-prices.ts:95 The usage row stamps one fixed label after the session; that label does not select a tier or an effort, and the model is chosen in the adapter.
app/_lib/voice/openai.ts:217 The only eagerness dial is semantic voice-activity detection, not a reasoning-effort setting on the model.
app/_lib/voice/provider-traits.ts:82 The free-provider must not fail onto a paid one is a conditional in the evaluator, not a data rule with an owner that warns at edit time.
app/_lib/voice/openai.ts:15 The model override is read from the environment inside the adapter, so it is an invisible global with no reaper.
app/_lib/voice/provider-traits.ts:25 Providers differ by wire transport, not by an ordinal model tier below which the interview still returns a plausible answer.
app/_lib/voice/connect-failover.ts:63 Failover to ElevenLabs still succeeds while that provider ignores the tool list the caller handed to every dial.
app/_lib/voice/minute-prices.ts:93 The ledger row takes the serving provider and a minute count; it has no policy version, rule chain, or failover flag.
app/_lib/voice/minute-prices.ts:81 Attribution identity is the trait the roster declares: the realtime model id, or else the ElevenLabs agent id, not a guess from behavior.
app/_lib/voice/minute-prices.ts:103 A completed billed session is recorded as ok without a check that the interview produced a usable answer, and failedOver never enters this row.

app/_lib/voice/connect-failover.test.ts:97 The transition is proven by a stubbed adapter test only; nothing states that this is the weaker, non-production claim, and there is no bounded live injection.
app/_lib/voice/provider-traits.ts:70 Alternate order is a fixed canonical list plus an availability filter, not a live score with a window and a sample size.
app/_lib/voice/minute-prices.ts:104 The usage row writes a success because the session was billed, so transport completion is stored as the outcome.
app/_lib/voice/connect-failover.ts:47 Substitution happens only when connect throws, before a session exists, so a live interview is not moved onto another model.

pairs.subject: model-routing
pairs.evidence: app/features/settings/models/ModelsRoutingPanel.tsx:14 The operator table pins a named provider and model string for each feature use case, which is the routing decision, and it does not map a closed call class to a tier and an effort.

techniques.evidence: app/features/settings/models/modelsRoutingSections.ts:1 The vocabulary is about twenty-five feature use cases, each pinned to a provider and model, which is a class per feature rather than a tier-and-effort pair.
app/features/settings/models/modelsRoutingActions.ts:18 A save preserves maxTokens and timeoutS and never sets reasoning effort, so a capped call inherits the provider default.
app/features/settings/models/ModelsRoutingPanel.tsx:141 Some use cases are bound to a call-site provider and model that this table cannot change, so not every call is decided at one door.
app/features/settings/models/ModelsRoutingRow.tsx:51 A call-site pin is shown as locked with no removal condition on this surface.
app/features/settings/models/ModelsRoutingRow.tsx:17 The floor named here is the deterministic template that served instead of a model, not a measured minimum tier the pin is forbidden to cross.
app/features/settings/models/modelsKeysPanelLogic.ts:79 A self-hosted endpoint is stored as a base URL on a provider row, with no declared dialect, context limit, or admission surface.

app/features/settings/models/ModelsQualityOverview.tsx:240 A routing change applies on one click; the stale-write check stops a lost update and is not a reviewed before/after diff or a policy version.
app/features/settings/models/modelsRoutingHealth.ts:82 Drift is raised only when the served provider differs; a different model on the pinned provider stays serving.
app/features/settings/models/modelsRoutingHealth.ts:18 The row classifies a finished ledger read; it does not decide whether a candidate can still be swapped before the first byte.
app/features/settings/models/modelsRoutingHealth.test.ts:3 The template fallback is something the ledger already recorded; this classifier does not inject or withhold the primary.
app/features/settings/models/ModelsQualityOverview.tsx:238 Order is a baked noise-band then minimum cost, not a live convex score with a named window and sample size.
app/_lib/llm-quality.ts:439 The pick the Pin button writes drops any model whose llmRate is under 0.9 before quality and cost are combined, so an operational ratio is a gate.
app/features/settings/models/ModelsTab.tsx:14 The decision this tab stores is a standing use-case pin; the directory has no prompt-prefix or mid-conversation swap.

pairs.registryProposal: turn-classification's three-to-five semantic classes and capability-floors' per-capability measurement pull apart: a product that measures breakage per capability, as this table does with one row per use case, has no legal place to put that row without either becoming a class-per-feature or hiding the floor inside a shared class.
